name: Granite-Chancel
specific_features: Natural granite amphitheater formation at the south pole
Mineral veins forming visible patterns across cliff faces
description: Granite-Chancel is a small rocky world whose surface is dominated by exposed granite batholiths, enormous intrusive igneous formations that have been laid bare by billions of years of erosion stripping away softer overlying rock. The granite ranges in color from pale gray to deep pink depending on feldspar content, creating a landscape of stark, geometric beauty. The low gravity has preserved formations that would have collapsed under heavier pull, arches and overhangs of stone spanning distances that defy terrestrial expectations.

The thin atmosphere supports minimal weather, but what exists is dominated by thermal cycling that slowly fractures the granite along crystal boundaries, producing angular rubble fields between the intact formations. Sound carries poorly in the thin air, reducing even close-range conversation to muffled exchanges. The mineral veins that thread through the granite glow faintly in certain wavelengths, trace radioactive elements producing a subtle luminescence visible only in the deep shadows of the graben valleys.

The south polar amphitheater is Granite-Chancel's most striking feature, a natural bowl formation three kilometers in diameter with terraced walls of exposed granite that bear an uncanny resemblance to constructed seating. The formation is entirely natural, created by differential erosion of a ring-shaped batholith, but its geometry is so regular that it has become a landmark for pilots navigating the system. Early surveyors used the amphitheater as a base camp, its walls providing shelter from the thermal extremes and micrometeorite strikes that characterize the surface.

The granite and associated minerals are of exceptional quality for construction applications, the slow cooling of the deep-seated batholiths producing crystal structures of unusual uniformity. Quarrying operations in the low gravity are efficient, large blocks lifted with minimal energy expenditure and launched to orbit by mass drivers that would be impractical on heavier worlds. Granite-Chancel has quietly become one of the sector's primary suppliers of dimension stone, its product found in structures across dozens of systems, each block carrying a piece of a world that looks like a church stripped to bare stone.
